rule_summary: Public monthly streaming tariff structure and domestic royalty-base rules load observable settlement pressure onto Korean music-streaming services
notes: Anchored to `creator_protective_institution_audit_log.md`: public monthly tariff and gross-sales-base structure are directly observable on the domestic side, but they do not by themselves prove direct foreign advantage.

rule_summary: Discount inclusion and related domestic settlement rules keep creator-protective payout logic inside the Korean streaming pricing structure
notes: Domestic rules can be described as creator-protective in orientation while still increasing Korean-platform burden incidence.

rule_summary: Same-service in-app settlement rule prevents automatic netting-out of app-store fee burden from the domestic royalty base
notes: This is the strongest mechanism linking creator-protective rules to domestic-platform burden in the Korean music market, but it still requires separate reach/tax lanes before inferring foreign advantage.

rule_summary: Domestic rights-governance verification and settlement transparency obligations raise compliance and verification friction for Korean platforms
notes: Use governance-friction and transparency logs as support. This is more about domestic verification burden than a clean rate gap.

rule_summary: Revenue-sharing sustainability and payout timing can transfer working-capital pressure from creators to domestic platforms or vice versa depending on settlement design
notes: Anchored to `webtoon_story_module_design_log.md`: currently framed as recovery-pressure and payout-timing bridge, not as a settled headline-ready incidence estimate.

rule_summary: Forced buyout, upside-sharing erosion, and unilateral-policy-change friction can harm creators while also creating platform-side bargaining or support burdens
notes: Anchored to `exploitative_upside_sharing_log.md`: important creator-side object but currently outside adopted quantitative language unless contract evidence is assembled.

rule_summary: Hold-up, settlement-transparency, and bargaining asymmetry questions remain qualitatively important but are not yet directly measured in a same-service foreign-comparator frame
notes: Anchored to `fgi_interview_guide_log.md`; this remains triangulation input, not direct quantified incidence.

rule_summary: Most digital-infra burden objects in the current report concern telecom/network/app-distribution regulation rather than creator/artist protection in a narrow sense
notes: Do not force digital-infra creator-incidence into the score when the protected group is not clearly creators/artists. If needed later, treat app-developer protection as a separate side object.
